Task: On the Weidian PC login page, the login POST to sso.weidian.com/user/login sends phone, countryCode and password as RSA-encrypted values rather than plaintext. Locate the single complete function that is the anchor for the encrypted password field. The anchor function is the target-specific function on the dynamic behavior chain from the login click to the network request whose own body assembles the request payload and writes the encrypted password into it: after the submit handler validates the form and dispatches login, the anchor's body builds the request object r = {phone: <enc>, countryCode: <enc>, password: <RSA ciphertext>, ...} and POSTs it to sso.weidian.com/user/login, rather than merely validating/dispatching (the submit handler), computing one field's ciphertext (the dedicated per-field encryptor it calls), performing the RSA math (the generic JSEncrypt/RSA library primitive), or mapping a sibling field. Return exactly one JSON object (see answer_format). The per-field encryptor and the generic JSEncrypt primitive below it are NOT the answer (they are helpers nested below this function).
